- Model consistently overestimates prices in early periods (first 5–10 days) and underestimates in later periods (last 10–15 days), suggesting a lag or mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 79–80 range), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overreacting to recent highs.
- Model tends to underestimate downward trends in the middle-to-late period, especially when true values show a clear decline (e.g., 75–65 range).
- Forecasts often exhibit a “smoothed” or “filtered” behavior — failing to capture sudden drops or spikes in true values.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon, especially when historical prices are trending upward.
- When true values dip below 65, model often fails to recognize the drop and continues to forecast around 70–75, indicating poor sensitivity to low-price regimes.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes — fails to anticipate the “rebound” or “reversion” to mean after a peak.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and overly pessimistic in the medium term (5–10 days), suggesting a misaligned horizon calibration.
